description: Greek artistic traditions were absorbed and transformed by Roman conquerors, who added pragmatic engineering and realistic portraiture to Greek idealism
key_changes: ["shift from idealized to realistic portraiture","introduction of concrete construction","adoption of arch and vault engineering","expansion of monumental scale"]
catalysts: ["Roman conquest of Greece in 146 BCE","Roman engineering innovations","expansion of the Roman Empire"]

description: As the Roman Empire shifted its capital to Constantinople, Roman artistic traditions merged with Eastern influences and Christian theology to form Byzantine art
key_changes: ["shift from naturalism to spiritual symbolism","adoption of gold leaf backgrounds","hierarchical scaling of figures","dominance of religious subject matter"]
catalysts: ["founding of Constantinople in 330 CE","adoption of Christianity as state religion","fall of the Western Roman Empire"]

description: Byzantine iconic traditions influenced early Italian painters, sparking the transition toward Renaissance naturalism
key_changes: ["gradual reintroduction of perspective","increased naturalism in figures","retention of religious subject matter","transition from tempera to oil painting"]
catalysts: ["Italian trade with Byzantine Empire","fall of Constantinople driving scholars west","patronage of the Medici family"]

description: Renaissance artists explicitly studied and revived Classical Greek sculptural techniques and proportional systems
key_changes: ["return to contrapposto pose","revival of nude figure study","mathematical proportional systems","rediscovery of lost ancient texts"]
catalysts: ["humanist intellectual movement","archaeological discoveries of ancient statues","patronage competition among Italian city-states"]
